text:
B: Hiya. Can you hear me? This really is my last one this time, I've checked properly.
A: Er, yeah. Yeah, fine. Gareth. Wrexham.
B: Joanne, Sutton-in-Ashfield. Oh, I've already had one Gareth today, the one from Essex.
A: Yeah, I had him an' all.
B: He was nice. Very, erm, well travelled.
A: Aye. Japan five times.
B: Five times! I've been to Skegness more than that, and that's about it.
A: Abersoch for us. Caravan park. Same one most summers.
B: Oh, I love Wales. We do a cheap week there sometimes, when we can. Is Abersoch right on the sea?
A: Yeah, on the Llŷn. Beach is just down the road. Kerry likes it, so.
B: Is Kerry your wife?
A: Yeah. She's a healthcare assistant up the Maelor. The hospital. She's on nights this week, so I'm sort of living on oven chips, you know.
B: Oh, bless you. I'd send you a cottage pie if I could. I always make too much anyway, Gary takes it for his dinner at work the next day. Sorry, he's my partner. He drives a forklift at a warehouse. You remind me of him a bit, actually, from your photo. That's meant nicely, I promise.
A: Ha. Fair enough.
B: What do you do yourself?
A: Transport office. Building supplies. Booking deliveries in, that sort of thing.
B: Oh, Gary'd know all about that. He's always moaning about lorries not turning up.
A: Yeah. That's most of my day, them not turning up.
B: I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school. Dinners, washing up, wiping the hall down after. It's busy at twelve but I like it, and it fits round term time. Sorry, I'm talking a lot. I always do when I'm nervous, I don't know if that makes sense.
A: Nah, you're alright. Kerry's the same.
B: Is that a dog bed I saw behind you?
A: Yeah. Dot. Staffy. She sulks when Kerry's on nights, sort of mopes about.
B: Aw. We've got a cat, Moss. She's old now, she sleeps on the shelf above the radiator all day. Doesn't sulk, she just looks at you like you've let her down.
A: Ha. Cats, yeah.
B: Can I ask you something daft? What do you call a bread roll? I've been asking everybody today.
A: Erm, a bap.
B: A bap! So that's cob, barm and bap now. The lad from Leicester said cob, thank goodness.
A: There's a van outside work does bacon baps on a Friday. Only Fridays, mind.
B: Oh, that's a nice thing to look forward to.
A: It is, yeah. Keeps me going, sort of.
B: Do you do anything at weekends, or is it the football?
A: Football, mostly. Wrexham. Go with my dad sometimes.
B: Gary's Mansfield. I go once a season and look at the birds on the stand roof. Honestly, I couldn't tell you the score most times, I just...
